reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring aphasia for left hemiparesis (use agnosia) or agnosia for right hemiparesis (use aphasia).
name: Rapid Arterial oCclusion Evaluation Scale

version.label: RACE (Pérez de la Ossa et al. 2014)
version.detail: Five NIHSS-derived items, 0–9. Aphasia is scored for right hemiparesis; agnosia for left hemiparesis.

purpose: Prehospital estimation of the likelihood of large vessel occlusion in suspected stroke.
intendedPopulation: Adults with suspected acute stroke, assessed by trained prehospital clinicians.

calculatorNotice.title: Screening scale
calculatorNotice.message: RACE estimates the likelihood of large vessel occlusion. Destination and treatment decisions follow regional protocols.

options.label: Normal to mild (holds more than 10 s)
Normal to mild (holds more than 5 s)
Present (eyes or head deviate to one side)

inputDefinitions.label: Aphasia (right hemiparesis) or agnosia (left hemiparesis)

options.label: Absent
options.detail: Follows both commands / recognises arm and its weakness.

options.label: Moderate
options.detail: Follows one command / does not recognise arm or is unaware of weakness.

options.label: Severe
options.detail: Follows neither command / does not recognise arm and is unaware of weakness.

inputDefinitions.help: Right hemiparesis: two commands (close your eyes, make a fist). Left hemiparesis: 'Whose arm is this?' and 'Can you move your arm?'.

resultStates.label: Below the derivation cut-off
resultStates.summary: Score 0–4: below the ≥5 cut-off used in the derivation study.
resultStates.detail: A lower score does not exclude stroke or large vessel occlusion.

resultStates.label: At or above the derivation cut-off
resultStates.summary: Score 5–9: in the derivation study, RACE ≥5 identified large vessel occlusion with sensitivity 0.85.
resultStates.detail: Integrate with the full assessment and the regional stroke pathway.

clinicalContext.text: Designed for prehospital use to estimate large vessel occlusion likelihood.

clinicalInsights.text: Posterior circulation occlusions may score low.
Re-assess on arrival; deficits can evolve during transport.

limitations.text: Does not distinguish ischaemic stroke from haemorrhage or mimics.

limitations: Accuracy depends on training and setting.

confounders.effect: Seizure, hypoglycaemia or migraine can produce scorable deficits.
Limits assessment of aphasia and agnosia.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Whether a vessel is actually occluded.

guideSections.what: A five-item prehospital scale derived from NIHSS items to estimate large vessel occlusion likelihood.
guideSections.whenToUse: Prehospital assessment of suspected stroke within a regional protocol.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score facial palsy, arm and leg motor function, head and gaze deviation, and either aphasia (right hemiparesis) or agnosia (left hemiparesis). Sum to 0–9.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A screening scale; confirmation requires vascular imaging.

sources.citation: Pérez de la Ossa N, Carrera D, Gorchs M, et al. Design and validation of a prehospital stroke scale to predict large arterial occlusion: the Rapid Arterial Occlusion Evaluation Scale. Stroke. 2014;45(1):87-91.
